summary: Cytoplasmic viscosity values relative to water exist as curated single numbers in BioNumbers (~20 entries, organism unspecified or cultured cells) and as a CC0 per-cell micropipette creep table for tumour cell lines; amoeboid deformation movies exist for Dictyostelium in the BioImage Archive; nothing public gives Amoeba proteus viscosity or creep under a calibrated pressure, which remains in the 1920s–1950s microrheology papers (Heilbrunn, Allen).
next_step: Compile the Amoeba/Physarum cytoplasm viscosity literature (Heilbrunn centrifuge, Allen, Yagi) into a table with method, length scale and temperature alongside the BioNumbers entries, and pair a Dictyostelium movie set with its traction-force data for a creep-timescale comparison.
obstacles_confirmed: Viscosities differ by method and are not gathered in one downloadable rheology table.
Public images seldom include calibrated applied pressure.
